agent.task: paging-audit-1b - Opus critic B, the systems designer: the handful of building blocks the system actually has, what is redundant, the organizing principle
agent.outcome: landed - the handful: one rectangle and six words over it - stage (the box a click changes the inside of; never moves), navigation (what a click on a child does + how children are drawn), content, room (the width word), arrangement (where the parts sit around the box), skin (surface + type scale). Five of six are shown; the stage - the realm's own rule - has no page, no chip, no single name (nine names in the code). Only build/ lets a reader configure or generate; nothing crosses two blocks except transitions (skin x navigation) - the owner's 'layouts x navigation x appearance x hierarchy' exists nowhere. Merge: navigation written three times (keep build/words.js NAVS); surfaces three times + a translation; arrangement five times (the layouts realm owns it); build/ supersedes make/'s editing (make = the file manager). Delete: critique/, inventory/ (site surveys), explorer/ (prose), center/, transitions/, the thirteen one-value dirs under styles/sizes/toolbars (one route() gives them urls), the xs-xl content axis. Missing: two independent colour controls, a combinator across all six, the preset library + dropdown, a page hosted inside a page, ext/drawer, the stable/dynamic label. Principle: the realm is ONE configurable page, not a directory of pages - six words, one stage, one control and one name each; every surviving directory is a preset that earned a url. Today: 16 trees, 50 directories, six things.

Keep: Templates, the tile grid's behaviour, Build's picture-choosers + live preview, Right nav. Measured: chips persist across refresh with a Modified alert - decision 4 not met. First screen wished for: no paragraph; four live miniatures full width under one caption each; the Templates shapes as pictures with 'pick a shape, then pick what a click does'; one compact grid of every page above the fold; docs one click down.
